title: OpenAI took the Apple lawsuit public and posted the receipts. Apple doubled down the same day.
excerpt: OpenAI aired private messages to rebut Apple's trade-secrets suit. The same day, Apple sought an injunction and said 11 more ex-staff may be involved.
content_html:
The legal fight between Apple and OpenAI turned public and personal this week. OpenAI published a blog post titled “Apple is getting this wrong,” airing private messages and emails to rebut Apple’s trade-secrets lawsuit. On the same day, Apple escalated in court. Two former partners are now trading blows in the open.

Apple sued in July, accusing OpenAI of profiting from secrets carried out by former Apple staff. OpenAI’s post called the suit “careless, aggressive and oddly personal,” and denied the core claim. “We do not have, nor want, any of their trade secrets,” it wrote.

OpenAI’s sharpest jab was about a mistake. Apple had said it contacted OpenAI in February and got no reply. OpenAI tells it differently.

It says Apple’s outside lawyer emailed its general counsel by accident, and claimed a phone call that never happened. The lawyer then admitted the message was meant for a different former Apple employee, surname Wang. OpenAI cast the mix-up as Apple “confusing two Asian last names,” and said it only surfaced when OpenAI flagged it.

The emails, which also appear in Apple’s own court filings, show the lawyer later apologising. Apple’s counsel had described itself as “resolving any issues,” OpenAI wrote. Then came roughly five months of silence before the lawsuit landed.

The bigger fight is over Chang Liu, a former iPhone engineer who left Apple in January. Apple says he tapped into confidential files after leaving. OpenAI published iMessages it says show the reverse. Apple employees, it says, asked Liu for help locating files after his last day.

The exchanges walk through airdrops and a still-signed-in iCloud account. In one, an Apple worker jokes about clicking “the sad button in workday” to log the departure.

OpenAI pins the blame on Apple’s own housekeeping. Departing staff keep “residual access,” it argued, because Apple fails to cut them off when they leave. Apple has also accused OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, Tang Tan, a 24-year Apple veteran, of soliciting secrets. OpenAI says Tan has always told his team not to touch rivals’ confidential information.

The receipts are a defence, not a verdict. The messages are OpenAI’s own selection, heavily redacted, and settle nothing on their own. But they hand the public a rare look inside a case both companies would normally fight behind closed doors.

Apple doubles down

Apple did not soften. On Monday it asked a federal judge for a preliminary injunction to bar OpenAI, Liu and Tan from using or disclosing its alleged secrets while the case runs. “If Apple’s trade secrets are used and spread throughout OpenAI, or get embedded in its products and operations, the damage cannot be undone,” its lawyers wrote.

It went further. Apple filed a second motion for expedited discovery and depositions. It also said its investigation had turned up 11 more former employees who may be involved. One allegedly met Liu before a colleague’s OpenAI interview and discussed unannounced products. Another, Apple says, took screenshots of confidential documents before interviewing there.

OpenAI called the injunction “based on false information and completely unnecessary,” and repeated that it wants none of Apple’s secrets. Apple did not respond to requests for comment.

What is actually at stake

Behind the filings is a partnership gone sour. OpenAI’s technology powers Apple Intelligence and Siri, and the two were close collaborators. The mood changed after OpenAI bought Jony Ive’s design studio io for $6.5bn and hired more than 400 former Apple staff to build its own devices. Apple, meanwhile, turned to Google to rebuild Siri.

Going public is the unusual part. Companies in active litigation rarely publish their evidence mid-case, and OpenAI’s post is a bid for the court of public opinion, not a legal filing. It changes nothing before the judge. What it does is let OpenAI tell its own story while Apple stays characteristically silent.

The clock is now set. OpenAI must file its formal response by 17 August, and the judge will hear the injunction on 1 October in a California federal court. Until then, two of the most valuable companies in technology are fighting in the open, with OpenAI’s hardware ambitions caught in the middle.

content_html_zh:
苹果和 OpenAI 之间的法律斗争本周变得公开化和个人化。 OpenAI 发表了一篇题为“苹果搞错了”的博文，通过私人信息和电子邮件反驳苹果的商业秘密诉讼。 同一天，苹果公司在法庭上升级。 两位前合伙人现在公开互殴。

苹果于 7 月提起诉讼，指控 OpenAI 从前苹果员工的机密中获利。 OpenAI 的帖子称该诉讼“粗心、咄咄逼人，而且非常个人化”，并否认了核心主张。 “我们没有、也不想要他们的任何商业秘密，”它写道。

OpenAI 最尖锐的攻击是关于一个错误。 苹果曾表示，它在 2 月份联系了 OpenAI，但没有得到回复。 OpenAI 的说法有所不同。

据称，苹果公司的外部律师无意中向其总法律顾问发送了电子邮件，并声称接到了从未打过的电话。 该律师随后承认，该消息是发给另一名王姓前苹果员工的。 OpenAI 将这种混淆视为苹果“混淆了两个亚洲姓氏”，并表示只有在 OpenAI 标记后才出现。

这些电子邮件也出现在苹果自己的法庭文件中，显示律师后来道歉。 OpenAI 写道，苹果的律师称自己“解决了任何问题”。 在诉讼落地之前，接下来是大约五个月的沉默。

更大的争论是围绕一月份离开苹果的前 iPhone 工程师刘畅展开的。 苹果公司表示，他在离开后查阅了机密文件。 OpenAI 发布了 iMessages，据说显示了相反的情况。 据称，苹果员工在刘先生去世后请求帮助查找文件。

交易所通过空投和仍登录的 iCloud 帐户进行操作。 在其中一篇文章中，一名苹果员工开玩笑说，点击“工作日中悲伤的按钮”来记录离职情况。

OpenAI 将责任归咎于苹果自己的内务管理。 它辩称，离职员工保留“剩余访问权限”，因为苹果未能在他们离开时切断他们的联系。 苹果还指控 OpenAI 首席硬件官、在苹果工作 24 年的资深人士唐坦索取机密。 OpenAI 表示，Tan 一直告诉他的团队不要接触竞争对手的机密信息。

收据是辩护，而不是判决。 这些消息是 OpenAI 自己选择的，经过大量编辑，并没有自行解决任何问题。 但他们让公众难得一睹这两家公司通常会闭门斗争的案件的内部情况。

苹果加倍降价

苹果并没有软化。 周一，该公司要求联邦法官发布初步禁令，禁止 OpenAI、Liu 和 Tan 在案件审理期间使用或披露其所谓的秘密。 “如果苹果的商业秘密在整个 OpenAI 中被使用和传播，或者被嵌入到其产品和运营中，那么损害就无法挽回，”其律师写道。

它更进一步。 苹果提出了第二项要求加快发现和证词的动议。 该公司还表示，调查还发现了另外 11 名可能参与其中的前雇员。 据称，其中一人在一位同事参加 OpenAI 面试之前见过刘，并讨论了未发布的产品。 苹果公司表示，另一名员工在面试前截取了机密文件的屏幕截图。

OpenAI 称该禁令“基于虚假信息，完全没有必要”，并重申它不想要苹果的任何秘密。 苹果没有回应置评请求。

真正的利害关系是什么

这些文件的背后是一种合作关系的恶化。 OpenAI 的技术为 Apple Intelligence 和 Siri 提供支持，两者是密切的合作伙伴。 在 OpenAI 以 65 亿美元收购 Jony Ive 的设计工作室 io 并聘请 400 多名前苹果员工来打造自己的设备后，人们的情绪发生了变化。 与此同时，苹果公司求助于谷歌来重建 Siri。

上市是不寻常的部分。 正在进行诉讼的公司很少在案件中途公布证据，而 OpenAI 的帖子是为了争取公众舆论，而不是法律备案。 它在法官面前没有任何改变。 它所做的就是让 OpenAI 讲述自己的故事，而苹果则保持一贯的沉默。

时钟现已设定。 OpenAI 必须在 8 月 17 日之前提交正式答复，法官将于 10 月 1 日在加州联邦法院听取该禁令。 在那之前，科技领域两家最有价值的公司正在公开战斗，OpenAI 的硬件野心被夹在中间。
